text:
ana: TL;DR — RFC suggests runtime <-> adapter capability negotiation so callers can pick graceful fallbacks for hosted/dedicated/private. Question: how far do we push capability discovery vs keeping adapter surface minimal?

matt: +1 on negotiating capabilities, but worried about attack surface and complexity for private deployments. we should gate sensitive capabilities behind authz.

siobhan: For Dedicated we need predictable SLOs. If caller sees capability X absent, fallback should choose variant with same latency profile, not just feature parity.

infra-bot: deploybot: Canary finished for canary-42. No regressions. :white_check_mark: 

ana: (oops) meant to say @matt — agree re authz. thinking: capability manifest that is signed by control plane for hosted, and by customer key for private. verification step before using advanced features.

devon: Signed manifests make sense. We also need a small, stable core API so adapters can always respond with a minimal success/fallback path. otherwise caller code explodes.

kevin: +1. propose surfaces: { "core": [generate, embeddings], "advanced": [kv-cache, prefix-cache, stateful-sessions], "ops": [metrics-forwarding, trace-headers] } as capabilities. keep names opaque and versioned.

siobhan: Also include performance hints: e.g. capability "kv-cache:v2" -> "avg-latency-ms: 1-3". caller can prefer lower-latency variants.

ana: example negotiation flow: 
```
client -> controlplane (route) -> adapter: "announce capabilities" (signed manifest)
adapter -> controlplane: hash(manifest)
client verifies manifest signature and picks model variant/fallback policy
```

matt: how do we prevent a private adapter from advertising capabilities it doesn't actually honor? signing by customer key helps but we need runtime probes. suggest periodic probe telemetry and a probe-first mode for new bindings.

olga: ops-side: we must avoid frequent probe storms. probes should be low-rate and sampled, and only on config changes. also add a probe health score that decays over time.

devon: runtime-probe idea: a small synthetic request that exercises the capability (e.g., prefix cache warm) and returns a timestamped signed assertion. if assertion fails, controlplane marks capability degraded.

kevin: what about evictions and fallbacks mid-request? if runtime loses a capability mid-stream (e.g., kv-cache OOM) we need deterministic fallback semantics — either fail fast or transparently route to compatible variant. prefer deterministic failover with metrics tagging.

siobhan: agree, deterministic failover. add a header/field in response: `x-redwood-fallback-reason: kv-cache-evicted` so callers and telemetry can correlate.

ana: security note: private deployments might not want signed manifests leaving their VPC. we should allow a policy: "local-only-manifests" where controlplane never fetches manifest, client validates solely with customer key material. document the trust assumptions clearly.

olga: ops: we'll need a way for SRE to opt out of auto-fallbacks in high-sensitivity tenants. config flag per-tenant: `auto_fallback: on|warn|off`.

matt: compatibility: manifest versions must be semver-like and include a stable subset id so older clients can still parse. avoid boolean flags for complex capabilities.

devon: implementation note: keep the negotiation layer as a thin protobuf layer with a well-defined wire contract. no business logic in negotiation — just capability exchange + signatures + health vector.

kevin: +1. Add audit events for manifest changes and fallback decisions. legal/compliance will want records if a customer opted out of telemetry.

ana: follow-ups: I'll draft a short RFC appendix with: manifest schema example, probe protocol, tenant flags, and a small reference JS snippet for clients. target next Wed for review.

siobhan: Thanks. please include fallback priority ordering example for latency-sensitive vs quality-sensitive routes.

infra-bot: ticket created: ARCH-1842 "capability-manifest-probe-and-fallbacks" — assigned to @ana. :spiral_note_pad: 

olga: one last ops ask — add a feature-flag to force "probe-first" for a tenant while migrating from private->dedicated; helps avoid surprises.

ana: noted, will add to appendix. :thumbsup: 

matt: overall +1. keep the negotiation surface tiny and auditable.

kevin: I'll sketch the telemetry fields and share in #eng-sre tomorrow.

ana: thanks everyone — will post RFC appendix PR once ready.
